  REGULAR MEETING OF THE
  SAN MARINO CITY COUNCIL
  WEDNESDAY, JUNE 10, 2026 AT 6:00 PM
  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  2200 HUNTINGTON DRIVE
  SAN MARINO, CA 91108
  AND
  HYATT CENTRIC GINZA
  6 CHOME-6-7 GINZA, CHUO CITY,
  TOKYO 104-0061, JAPAN

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council
with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically,
adjourned meetings are held on the last Friday of every month at 8:30 a.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City Clerk via email at CityClerk@SanMarinoCA.gov or by phone at (626)
300-0705 48 hours prior to the meeting for assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City
will do it’s best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

How to view or listen to the meeting from home:
  Visit www.SanMarinoCA.gov/Zoom

AGENDA – JUNE 10, 2026  PAGE 1 of 6
 How to offer public comment from home:
Public comment will be accepted by email to CityClerk@SanMarinoCA.gov until 3:00 p.m.
the day before the meeting. Written public comment received by 3:00 p.m. will be
distributed to City Council during the meeting. Any comments received after 3:00 p.m. will
be included in the public comment record but not provided to City Council at the meeting.

Written public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us teleconference
module during the meeting. Written Zoom comments will be accepted after the in-person
comments. Written Zoom comments will be read or summarized, then printed and made
part of the public record for the meeting.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

Council Member Chang, Council Member Chou, Council Member Shepherd Romey, Vice
Mayor Lo, Mayor Chou

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall,
2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the
Stoneman Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
https://www.SanMarinoCA.gov.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council by
completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. At
this time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on the agenda.
Pursuant to state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on issues not on the
meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor reserves the right to
place limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such items.

CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

This is an opportunity for the City Manager to inform the City Council and the public of any
upcoming events or matters of interest to the community.

  PRESENTATION

 PRESENTATION OF CERTIFICATES OF RECOGNITION FOR OUTGOING

AGENDA – JUNE 10, 2026  PAGE 2 of 6
  ADVISORY BODY MEMBERS

  PUBLIC HEARINGS

 1.  CONSIDERATION OF AN APPEAL OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S
  DECISION TO DENY  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DR 22-26 AT 535
  OLD MILL ROAD TO THE DEMOLISH AN EXISTING 1,751 SQUARE-
  FOOT RESIDENCE AND CONSTRUCT A NEW TWO-STORY 2,690
  SQUARE-FOOT RESIDENCE WITH A DETACHED TWO-CAR GARAGE
  (CHAN)

  Recommendation: Based on the information submitted to the record, staff
  recommends that the City Council: (1) determine that based on the whole of the
  administrative record, that the proposed addition is exempt from CEQA pursuant to
  State CEQA Guidelines, Article 19, Section 15301, Class 1 & Class 3, and that there is
  no substantial evidence demonstrating an exception to the categorical exemption
  pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15300.2 applies; (2) find that the proposed
  project meets the required findings; and (3) approve the project. If the City Council
  concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to adopt City Council Resolution No. R-26-21 approving the project as
  presented and find that the proposed project meets the required findings and
  determine that based on the whole of the administrative record, that the proposed
  addition is exempt from CEQA pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines, Article 19, Section
  15301, Class 1 & Class 3, and that there is no substantial evidence demonstrating an
  exception to the categorical exemption pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15300.2
  applies.”

  If the City Council affirms the adoption of Planning Commission Resolution No. PCR
  26-17, the appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to adopt City Council Resolution No. R-26-21 affirming the adoption of
  Planning Commission Resolution No. PCR 26-17 to deny Design Review Case Number
  DR-22-26 at 535 Old Mill Road to demolish an existing 1,751 sq ft single-family
  residence and construct a 2,690 sq ft two-story residence with a detached 2-car
  garage.”

  NEW BUSINESS

 2.  APPROVAL AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTIONS PERTAINING TO THE
  GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION TO BE HELD ON NOVEMBER 3, 2026

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council adopt: (1) Resolution No. R-26-
  15 calling and giving notice of the holding of a General Municipal Election to be held
  on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, for the election of certain officers as required by the
  provisions of the laws of the State of California relating to General Law Cities and

AGENDA – JUNE 10, 2026  PAGE 3 of 6
   requesting the Registrar of Voters of the County of Los Angeles to conduct said
  election; (2) Resolution No. R-26-16 requesting the Board of Supervisors of the
  County of Los Angeles to render services to the City relating to the conduct of a
  General Municipal Election to be held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026; (3) Resolution
  No. R-26-17 adopting regulations for candidates for elective office pertaining to
  candidates’ statements submitted to the voters at an election to be held on
  November 3, 2026; and (4) direct staff to return to a future City Council meeting with
  the necessary documents and ballot language to consider placing the City’s expiring
  Utility Users Tax on the November 3, 2026 ballot. If the Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to (1) adopt Resolution No. R-26-15, calling and giving notice of the holding
  of a General Municipal Election to be held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026; (2)
  Resolution No. R-26-16, requesting the Board of Supervisors of the County of Los
  Angeles to render services to the City relating to the conduct of a General Municipal
  Election to be held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026; (3) Resolution No. R-26-17,
  adopting regulations for candidates for elective office pertaining to candidates’
  statements submitted to the voters at the election to be held on November 3, 2026;
  and (4) direct staff to return to a future City Council meeting with the necessary
  documents and ballot language to consider placing the City’s expiring Utility Users
  Tax on the November 3, 2026 ballot.”

 3.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. R-26-07 ADOPTING PROCEDURES
  REQUIRED BY GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 54953.4 (SB 707)
  PERTAINING TO DISRUPTION OF TELEPHONIC OR INTERNET
  SERVICE

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council adopt Resolution No. R-26-07
  Adopting Procedures Required by Government Code Section 54953.4 (SB 707)
  Pertaining to Disruption of Telephonic or Internet Service. If the Council concurs with
  staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to adopt Resolution No. R-26-07 Adopting Procedures Required by
  Government Code Section 54953.4 (SB 707) Pertaining to Disruption of Telephonic or
  Internet Service.”

  CONSENT CALENDAR

 4.  APPROVE  A  PUBLIC WORKS  AGREEMENT  WITH  TRI-TECH
  RESTORATION IN THE AMOUNT OF $808,953.79 FOR WINDSTORM-
  RELATED ROOF REPAIRS TO CITY FACILITIES AND AUTHORIZE THE
  PARKS, AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE THE
  AGREEMENT ON BEHALF OF THE CITY, AND AUTHORIZE THE PUBLIC
  WORKS DIRECTOR/CITY ENGINEER TO APPROVE CONTRACT CHANGE
  ORDERS NECESSARY FOR THE COMPLETION OF THE PROJECT,
  SUBJECT TO CONCURRENCE BY THE CALIFORNIA JOINT POWERS
  INSURANCE AUTHORITY (CJPIA), WITH ALL ASSOCIATED COSTS
  FUNDED BY CJPIA

AGENDA – JUNE 10, 2026  PAGE 4 of 6
   Recommendation: Staff recommend that the City Council (1) approve a Public Works
  Agreement with Tri-Tech Restoration in the amount of $808,953.79 for roof repairs at
  Lacy Park and City Hall and (2) authorize the City Manager to execute the Agreement
  on behalf of the City, and (3) authorize the Parks and Public Works Director/City
  Engineer to approve contract change orders necessary for the completion of the
  project, subject to concurrence by CJPIA, with all costs to be paid by CJPIA as
  outlined in the agreement. If the Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an
  appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to (1) approve a Public Works Agreement with Tri-Tech Restoration in the
  amount of $808,953.79 for windstorm-related roof repairs to City facilities, (2)
  authorize the City Manager to execute the Agreement on behalf of the City, and (3)
  authorize the Parks and Public Works Director/City Engineer to approve contract
  change orders necessary for the completion of the project, subject to concurrence by
  the California Joint Powers Insurance Authority (CJPIA), with all costs funded by
  CJPIA.”

 5.  REPORT ON EMERGENCY ACTIONS TAKEN TO REPAIR/REMEDIATE
  FIRE STATION 91 AND REQUEST TO EXTEND EMERGENCY
  PROCUREMENT PURSUANT TO PUBLIC CONTRACTS CODE SECTION
  22050 AND SAN MARINO MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 2.06.05(A)(8)

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council receive the report of
  repair/remediation actions undertaken to date and extend the emergency by a 4/5
  vote to facilitate expeditious restoration of Fire Station 91. If the City Council concurs
  with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  "I move to receive and file the report of repair/remediation actions undertaken to
  date and to extend the emergency action approved in Resolution No. R-26-08 to
  facilitate the expeditious restoration of Fire Station 91."

 6.  RECEIVE AND FILE MONTHLY DISBURSEMENTS REPORT FOR MAY
  2026

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file the Monthly
  Disbursements Report for the month of May 2026. If the City Council concurs with
  staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the Monthly Disbursements Report for the month of May
  2026.”

 7.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the May 2026 Minutes. If
  the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would
  be:

  “I move to approve the Minutes of the Special Meeting of May 13, 2026, the Regular
  Meeting of May 13, 2026, and the Adjourned Regular Meeting of May 29, 2026.”

AGENDA – JUNE 10, 2026  PAGE 5 of 6
 WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTION

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City
received by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of San
Marino to at least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be
made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San
Marino, California 91108, and will also be included in the public agenda packet that will
available for review at the City Council meeting.
